transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-29
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Markus Heller (CTO - Celestia), Lena Ortiz (Platform Eng - Celestia), Samir Rao (ML Eng - Celestia)

Summary: Quick discovery to nail down Celestia's p95 SLOs, concurrency targets, streaming first-token vs full completion latency, and decide whether Hosted or Dedicated (or Private) makes sense. Agreed to run a focused benchmark and exchange security docs.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Jordan from Redwood, AE, joining with Priya our SE. How's the morning/afternoon?
[00:06] Markus: Morning, thanks. Markus here. Quick context, we're migrating several chat endpoints off a homegrown infra and need to validate options.
[00:12] Priya: Great, Markus. Can you kick off with your current SLOs and traffic shape? Even ballpark is fine.
[00:18] Lena: Sure. For our customer-facing chat, we need p95 first-token <= 200ms ideally, and p95 for full response under 1.2s for avg 400-token completions. Concurrency peaks around 150 concurrent streams, sustained at ~60.
[00:30] Samir: On batch endpoints (summarization), we do higher throughput — up to 2k tokens/sec aggregate during batch windows. We're also doing streaming for low-latency UX.
[00:40] Jordan: Ok that's helpful. So first-token p95 200ms is pretty strict. Out of interest, which models are you evaluating? Size and quantization matter a lot.
[00:48] Markus: Right now we're testing a 7B open model and a tuned 13B for production. We're open to quantized variants if quality holds.
[00:56] Priya: Good, that lines up. For hosted Redwood, our streaming first-token tends to be optimized for small-medium models with our inference runtime; for larger 13B models we see higher base latency but we can hit 200-300ms first-token with the right config and caching. Dedicated gives you more predictable p95s across sustained concurrency.
[01:12] Lena: Can you clarify caching? We heard about 'KV cache' but not sure how it works for streaming.
[01:18] Priya: Sure — KV cache is for prefix/multi-turn caching. If you have repeated context patterns, we can cache decoder keys to avoid re-compute, which reduces per-token latency. It helps throughput when many users share similar prompts. In streaming, first-token latency mostly depends on model load and scheduling, but subsequent tokens benefit more from cache and batching.
[01:32] Samir: Ok. We're also worried about tail latency under concurrency. At peak 150 streams, we need p95 to stay under target. Do you have examples or benchmarks?
[01:40] Jordan: We have benchmark decks. I'll share targeted scripts. But quick answer: on Dedicated with 8xA100-equivalent, teams hitting 150 concurrent small streams with a 7B quantized model see p95 first-token ~120-180ms and sustained tokens/sec ~1.2k-2k depending on batch config. Hosted is more variable under noisy neighbors.
[01:58] Markus: That sounds promising. What's the tradeoff in cost / procurement?
[02:04] Priya: Dedicated is a reserved capacity model — higher committed cost but predictable performance and isolation. Hosted is pay-as-you-go; cheaper for low sustained but can spike latency under heavy system-wide demand. Private/VPC gives you the control for compliance but adds ops work and minimum sizing.
[02:20] Lena: Security is non-negotiable. We need SOC2, KMS + HSM details, audit logs, and SSO/SAML for RBAC. Can you share docs?
[02:28] Jordan: Absolutely. I'll send the SOC2 pack and our KMS integration notes after this call.
[02:34] Samir: For the benchmark, can you support streaming test harness? We want to measure first-token p95, and then p95 for full response, and tokens/sec under concurrency.
[02:42] Priya: Yes. We can provide a perf script that simulates 50, 150, and 200 concurrent streams, and measures first-token and inter-token time, and also a separate load for batch summarization to capture tokens/sec. We'll run with your prompt set so it's realistic.
[02:56] Markus: What about quantization? We saw some quality drop with int8 on our tuned model. Can Redwood recommend quantization levels?
[03:04] Priya: We have profiles per-model. We'll run A/B with int8 and Q4_0 where supported, and report quality diffs on your eval prompts. Sometimes hybrid strategies (int8 for non-critical paths) work. We'll surface exact delta in the benchmark report.
[03:18] Jordan: Also routing/fallback: if Dedicated has transient capacity issues, Redwood can auto-fallback to hosted variant or a smaller model to keep latency SLOs — there's a policy layer for that.
[03:28] Lena: That fallback capability is interesting; helps during traffic bursts. We have a question about networking — VPC peering for Private deployment: does Redwood support customer-managed NAT and HSM?
[03:36] Priya: Yes for Private we support customer-managed networking and HSM/KMS integrations. For Hosted and Dedicated, we offer VPC peering and private connectivity options, and KMS for key wrapping. We'll include the networking diagram in the security pack.
[03:48] Samir: Any gotchas on streaming token/sec numbers? We need to understand sustained tokens/sec per GPU vs aggregate.
[03:54] Priya: It varies by model and sequence length. For example, a quantized 7B might do ~1.5k tokens/sec on a single GPU in streaming mode with efficient kernels; a 13B might be 600-900 tokens/sec. With batching across concurrent streams you can get higher aggregate throughput but at the cost of slightly higher per-token latency for some requests.
[04:12] Markus: So for our target — 150 concurrent streams, avg 400-token completion — what's realistic p95 and cost estimate?
[04:20] Priya: Ballpark: Dedicated with properly sized pool and autoscaling tuned for streaming you can expect p95 first-token ~150-250ms and p95 full completion under ~1.5s for 7B; for 13B expect p95s higher, maybe 400-800ms first-token unless you heavily optimize. We'll produce exact numbers in the benchmark.
[04:40] Lena: How long does a benchmark take and what do you need from us?
[04:44] Priya: Typically ~1 hour per configuration (model + concurrency profile). We'll need your representative prompt set (ideally 100-200 prompts), sequence length distribution, and a traffic CSV with concurrency over time. Also network egress constraints if any.
[04:58] Jordan: We'll also send pricing for Dedicated vs Hosted for the anticipated baseline load. That helps you compare cost-per-1k tokens and reserved commit.
[05:06] Markus: One more question: how accurate are the Fireflies transcript metrics? (laughs)
[05:10] Jordan: (laughs) We try — but yes, the transcript can be noisy. We'll include the raw perf logs.
[05:14] Samir: Cool. On the security side, if we go for Dedicated in a cloud tenancy, do you support customer-managed KMS keys for encryption at rest?
[05:22] Priya: Yes — both Dedicated and Private can integrate with customer KMS; for Private you can control keys fully.
[05:28] Lena: Ok let's summarize next steps.
[05:30] Jordan: Recap: Priya will run the 1-hour latency and tokens/sec benchmarks using Celestia's prompts at 50 and 150 concurrent streams, and a 200-concurrency stress run. Jordan will share security docs and pricing. Customer to share prompt set and traffic profile by 2026-12-31. Any objections?
[05:46] Markus: No objections. Sounds good.
[05:48] Priya: Quick note — we'll also include guidance on batching/caching configs and quantization recommendations we touched on.
[05:56] Jordan: Perfect. We'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark results review and the Dedicated pricing deep dive. Thanks all.
[06:02] Lena: Thanks, bye.
[06:04] Markus: Bye.

(Transcript ends — automated timestamps are approximate; some words may be mis-transcribed.)
